noted_behavior: Best performer (rubric). 1M steps + CNN + moderate lr: strong exploration-exploitation balance; agent tracks ball and scores often. Main model for play.py.
Lower LR hurts sample efficiency: updates too small for visible improvement in 150k steps; paddle jitters and misses fast returns. Illustrates lr vs learning speed trade-off.
Total failure vs CNN (architecture). MLP on flattened pixels ignores spatial layout; policy never learns reliable pursuit. Documents why CNNPolicy fits screen-based Atari.

Higher LR (2e-4): faster early Q-updates than 1e-4 baseline; monitor stability and eval variance vs exp01—risk of noisier targets if lr too aggressive. Replace NA with eval_mean/std after EvalCallback run.
Lower gamma (0.95): more myopic credit assignment than gamma=0.99; discounts future rallies—useful contrast for discount-factor discussion. Replace NA with eval_mean/std after you run this sweep.
Higher gamma (0.999): stronger long-horizon value signal vs 0.99; compare learning speed and stability to exp01. Trade-off: very long credit paths can slow early learning on short horizons.
Batch 64: smoother gradient estimates than 32 but fewer noisy updates per timestep—classic batch size vs update noise trade-off; performance near baseline at 150k.
Batch 128 + higher epsilon_end (0.1): stable learning but slower improvement vs smaller batch + default epsilon; exploration-exploitation and batch size interact.
300k with tighter epsilon_end (0.01) and longer exploration_fraction (0.2): shorter total budget than exp01; compare final skill and late-game greed to exp01/exp10.
500k with faster epsilon decay fraction (0.05): strong play and often beats opponent; slightly less consistent than full 1M (exp01). Shows timestep budget vs final performance.
